assumptions.text: The HTML-stripped PBI description file named in the task brief (tool-results/130949.desc.txt) did not exist on disk when this analysis ran. The inventory was therefore built from the QA Manager's written SCOPE brief (surfaces, objects/components, roles, lifecycle, the full character-limit table, file type/size validation rules, bilingual and responsive requirements) plus the verified Figma digest and layout tokens. Every inventory row traces to a statement in that brief or to verified design; nothing was invented. If the raw description contains field-level detail the brief did not summarise (for example exact validation message wording, or a max on a field listed here as unlimited), this set must be re-diffed against it before injection.

has_ac = FALSE. The Azure AC field literally contains the string 'No AC'. Zero AC-n rows and an empty ac_clause_map were produced deliberately; the Given/When/Then prose inside the description body was routed to OBJ-n / FLD-n / CTL-n / ST-n / ROL-n / MSG-n / SUR-n / LNG-n / ENV-n instead. An AC-n row here would be a hard E5 gate failure.

The PBI's hero has no CTAs at all — this is stale copy carried over from the Legal Consultation page. No CTA cases were derived. TC-013 asserts positively that no CTA button renders in the hero; if the client actually wants CTAs here, TC-013 fails by design and CTA field/control inventory rows must be added. Needs a product decision.

DESIGN EXTRA: the sticky section index in the design lists seven entries (01 Overview, 02 Service information, 03 Downloadable resources, 04/05/06 'Frequently asked questions', 07 a duplicate 'Overview') while the PBI defines only 01-03. No cases were derived for 04-07 and TC-004 asserts the index contains EXACTLY the three PBI-defined entries. Needs a product decision.

DESIGN EXTRA: both resource cards render a '50 Downloads' / '50 تنزيل' counter (Cairo 400 14px/22px #A8A8A7). The PBI's resource field table has no download-counter field. No inventory row and no case was derived for it; TC-011 and TC-012 assert the PBI-defined metadata (title, File Type 'PDF', File Size '200 KB', download label) without asserting a counter. Needs a product decision on whether a download counter is in scope for this page.

DESIGN DEFECT, recorded not tested: the 'Supporting information' group in every frame repeats two bullets that belong to 'Preparing your proposal' — 'The expected value or potential benefit of the study.' and 'Available data, references, or supporting information.' TC-009 asserts the four bullets the PBI defines for that group and asserts that those two duplicated bullets do NOT appear. Raise the duplication with design separately.

DESIGN DEFECT, recorded not tested: an Arabic field label 'تاريخ الميلاد' with a red asterisk (#E11D48) appears in the newsletter/footer area of the ENGLISH frames (2824:38277 and 2824:38330), alongside placeholder hint copy 'This is a hint text to help user.' This is a shared newsletter-component default, not this page's authored content, so no case asserts on it. Worth raising with design/dev separately.

DESIGN DEFECT, already logged on PBI 130703: the shared Breadcrumb component instance carries the garbled default override 'Hcvxcxvcome' (rendered in the frames as a stale 'Item-3' trail). TC-003 asserts the breadcrumb reads 'Home > Services' per the PBI and explicitly asserts that no 'Hcvxcxvcome' or 'Item-3' node is rendered. The design-side defect is flagged separately, not re-filed here.

The PBI states that validation blocks save/publish but does not quote the literal validation strings for most fields. Only MSG-1..MSG-4 are stated as behaviours. Negative field cases therefore assert the observable outcome ('save is blocked and the field is flagged as required / over the limit') and never invent specific message wording.

The BRD does not specify a browser/version support matrix (background.md flags this as an open item). ENV-1..ENV-5 map exactly to the five verified Figma frames; ENV-6 (tablet 768px) is derived from the PBI's stated desktop/tablet/mobile responsive requirement and has no frame to assert tokens against, so TC-024 asserts reflow and legibility rather than exact tokens. No browser-specific rows were invented.

Character limits are applied exactly as the PBI's field table gives them: eyebrow 60, page title 100, fact label 60, fact value 120, section title 100, card title 100, group label 120, group item label 300, resource title 200, download label 40. The PBI does not state whether an over-limit value is REJECTED or silently TRUNCATED at input; every max+1 case asserts that the field does not accept a value longer than the limit — either input stops at the limit or save is blocked with the field flagged — which passes under either implementation. Confirm the intended behaviour if a stricter assertion is wanted.

'Positive integer' is the only stated Display Order constraint, so each Display Order field gets a valid case and a zero/negative invalid case. Decimal input, very large values and duplicate-value tie-breaking are unspecified; the duplicate-value case is carried as an EDGE case (TC-165) precisely because the PBI states no tie-break rule.

No maximum item count is stated for any repeatable collection (quick facts, sections, info cards, information groups, group items, resources). Add/reorder cases assume the authored counts (4 quick facts, 3 sections, 3 info cards, 2 groups, 6+4 bullets, 2 resources) and no upper-bound boundary case was produced, since inventing one would be invented scope.

Two business rules meet on the same input and the PBI does not say which wins: (a) a missing translation falls back to the current/default language, and (b) publish is blocked when Arabic is enabled and a mandatory Arabic value is missing. TC-162 tests the fallback on an OPTIONAL/non-blocking field and TC-163 tests the publish block on a MANDATORY field. Confirm this split matches the intended behaviour.

File constraints used in cases: hero banner JPG/PNG/SVG under 2 MB (disallowed sample .bmp, oversize sample 3 MB); resource file PDF only, 5 MB ceiling (disallowed sample .docx, oversize sample 6 MB). These come from the PBI's stated validation table; the specific rejected-sample formats are this analysis's choice and can be swapped for whatever samples the test data set holds.

Per this project's standards.md, every content operation on an Object-Definition-backed record runs through Object Authoring (https://qcdev.ihorizons.com/object-authoring), never Content & Data, and every draft/unpublish/preview public-visibility assertion runs in a fresh logged-out browser context. All Control_Panel cases here are written on that basis. Whether the Proposal for Research page is Object-Definition-backed or a plain Journal/Web Content article (as the Home Contact Us Section turned out to be) is not yet confirmed live — verify before automating.

Restricted-role cases (TC-026..TC-029) use the named CMS role accounts from standards.md (Site Content Editor test1@xyz.com, Site Content Author Test2@xyz.com) resolved via config.settings.cms_role_credentials(), never TEST_USER. The Site-Content-Editor DENIED case (TC-027) asserts that the Editor role does not grant Control Panel user/role administration — this is standard Liferay RBAC rather than an explicit PBI statement; confirm it is the intended denial boundary for this feature.

The public URL used throughout (/en/our-services/information/proposal-for-research and its /ar counterpart) is derived from the BRD's site structure; substitute the real friendly URL before execution.
